data: PhysioNet Sleep-EDF Expanded, sleep-cassette; channels Fpz-Cz, Pz-Oz, EOG horizontal
question: With enough records and the transition off-centre, does the geodesic CUSUM localize sleep transitions better than a log-total-power CUSUM?
verdict: PRIMARY (pre-registered, record level) INCONCLUSIVE -- manifold 59/151 vs scalar 67/151 (manifold-only 28, scalar-only 36, McNemar p = 0.382). Subject level (one record per subject, secondary): INCONCLUSIVE -- manifold 32/78 vs scalar 42/78 (manifold-only 12, scalar-only 22, McNemar p = 0.121). EEG only, no EOG (secondary): INCONCLUSIVE -- manifold 57/151 vs scalar 66/151 (manifold-only 30, scalar-only 39, McNemar p = 0.336); subject level 30/78 vs 39/78 (INCONCLUSIVE). Off-centre sanity: the centre-prior detector scores 0/151. Stopping rule: 153 of 153 SC recordings were available and analysed once; 151 had a qualifying transition.
